pipe-manifold.context: A horizontal header pipe with three branch pipes hanging below it, each with a valve. People use it for piping layouts, plant schematics and fluid distribution.

oil-pipeline.context: A raised pipe running across the ground on H-shaped supports and shrinking toward the horizon. It stands for oil and gas transport and long distance piping.

venturi-tube.context: A tube that narrows in the middle with two upright gauge tubes at different heights. It shows pressure change in flowing fluid and is used in physics and flow measurement.

spherical-storage-tank.context: A large round tank standing on straight legs with a band around its middle. It is the usual picture of gas storage at refineries and chemical plants.

oil-drum.context: An upright steel drum with two raised rings and a small bung on the lid. It stands for barrels of oil, fuel and chemicals.

ibc-tote.context: A cube plastic tank inside a metal grid cage on a pallet, with a small valve at the bottom. It represents intermediate bulk containers used to move liquids.

bulk-bag.context: A large square woven sack with a lifting loop at each top corner. It stands for bulk handling of sand, grain, cement and other loose goods.

air-cargo-container.context: An aircraft cargo container with one slanted top corner and a curtain door on the front. It is used for air freight, luggage handling and airport logistics.

rail-tank-car.context: A railway wagon carrying a long cylindrical tank with a dome on top, riding on two wheel sets. It stands for liquid freight by rail.

hopper-wagon.context: An open railway wagon with sloping ends that narrow into two chutes underneath. It carries loose bulk goods such as coal and grain and unloads from below.

radioactive-waste-drum.context: A steel drum marked with a radiation trefoil symbol. It stands for nuclear waste storage and hazardous material handling.

robotic-arm.context: An industrial robot arm on a low base with two jointed segments and a claw gripper at the end. It is used for factory automation and assembly lines.

robotic-gripper.context: Two parallel fingers closing on a small cube under a wrist block. It shows how a robot picks up and holds parts.

vacuum-gripper.context: A robot wrist with a row of suction cups lifting a flat box. It stands for vacuum picking in packaging and palletizing.

robotic-hand.context: A mechanical hand with jointed fingers and a pivot dot at each knuckle. It is used for humanoid robots, prosthetics and dexterous manipulation.

scara-robot.context: A short column carrying two horizontal links hinged end to end, with a vertical spindle at the tip. It is the classic assembly robot for fast pick and place work.

delta-robot.context: A top plate with three thin arms coming down to a small tool plate. It stands for fast parallel robots used in food and packaging lines.

automated-guided-vehicle.context: A low flat cart on small wheels carrying a box, with a sensor on the front. It stands for driverless transport in warehouses and factories.

delivery-robot.context: A small six-wheeled box robot with a lid and a flag on a thin antenna. It stands for sidewalk delivery of food and parcels.

robot-dog.context: A four-legged robot with a boxy body, a sensor head and legs bent backward. It stands for legged inspection robots and robotic pets.

teach-pendant.context: A handheld robot controller with a screen, a few keys and a round emergency stop button on the top corner. It is used to program and jog industrial robots.

programmable-logic-controller.context: A rail-mounted controller module with screw terminals along the top and bottom and small status lights. It stands for industrial automation control.

proximity-sensor.context: A threaded cylindrical sensor with lock nuts, a cable out the back and sensing waves in front of its face. It detects nearby metal objects without touching them.

limit-switch.context: A small box switch with a pivoting lever arm and a roller wheel at its tip. It tells a machine when a moving part has reached the end of its travel.

emergency-stop-button.context: A large mushroom-head push button on a round plate. It is the red button that shuts a machine down in an emergency.

start-stop-buttons.context: A control box with a solid start button marked I above a ring-shaped stop button marked O. It stands for motor control stations and machine operator panels.

safety-light-curtain.context: Two posts facing each other with horizontal beams drawn between them. It stands for the optical safety barrier that stops a machine when someone reaches in.

rfid-tag.context: A thin card with a coiled antenna around a tiny chip. It stands for radio tags used to track stock, parcels and access.

offshore-wind-turbine.context: A three-blade wind turbine on a tall tower rising out of wavy water lines. It stands for wind farms built at sea.

vertical-axis-wind-turbine.context: A tall mast with curved blades bowing out from top and bottom like an eggbeater. It stands for vertical axis wind turbines used on rooftops and in towns.

solar-power-tower.context: A tall tower with a round receiver on top and rows of tilted mirrors on posts facing it. It stands for concentrated solar power plants.

pelton-wheel.context: A wheel with cup-shaped buckets around its rim and a water jet hitting one bucket. It is the impulse turbine used in high-head hydropower.

tidal-turbine.context: A two-blade turbine on a pillar standing on the seabed beneath wave lines. It stands for power taken from tidal currents.

geothermal-plant.context: A low power plant building with steam plumes rising from vents and pipes running down into the ground. It stands for electricity and heat taken from the earth.

nuclear-reactor.context: A domed containment building with a radiation trefoil on its front. It stands for nuclear power stations and reactors.

nuclear-fuel-rods.context: A bundle of long thin rods held together by two horizontal grid spacers. It shows a fuel assembly from a nuclear reactor core.

tokamak.context: A donut-shaped fusion chamber seen at an angle and wrapped in evenly spaced coils. It stands for magnetic confinement fusion research.

hydrogen-fuel-cell.context: A stack of plates between two thick end plates, with a gas arrow going in and a water drop coming out. It stands for fuel cells that turn hydrogen into electricity.

hydrogen-tank.context: A tall capsule-shaped pressure tank with a valve on top and the letter H on its side. It stands for hydrogen storage for vehicles and plants.

grid-battery-storage.context: A container-sized box with a vent grille on one end and a large battery symbol on its side. It stands for grid-scale battery storage.

biofuel.context: An oil drop with a small leaf growing from its side. It stands for fuels made from plants such as biodiesel and ethanol.

power-transformer.context: A utility transformer tank with cooling fins on both sides and three bushings on top. It stands for high-voltage transformers in power networks.

electrical-substation.context: A fenced yard with two gantry posts, a transformer between them and wires strung overhead. It stands for substations in the power grid.

ceramic-insulator.context: A vertical string of ribbed disc insulators hanging from a bracket with a clamp at the bottom. It stands for the insulators on high-voltage power lines.

knife-switch.context: A hinged metal blade lever on an insulating base, swinging toward a spring clip. It stands for manual disconnect switches and open circuits.

three-phase-plug.context: A round industrial plug with a thick collar and five pins arranged in a circle. It stands for three-phase power connectors on site and in workshops.

tesla-coil.context: A tall coil tower topped by a ring with jagged lightning bolts arcing out. It stands for high-voltage spark demonstrations and electricity experiments.

geiger-counter.context: A handheld box with a dial meter, connected by a cable to a wand probe. It stands for radiation detection and measurement.

thermocouple.context: A thin probe with two wires twisted together at the tip and a flat two-pin plug at the other end. It stands for temperature sensors used in furnaces, ovens and process equipment.

mine-headframe.context: A tall A-frame steel tower with two wheels on top over a vertical shaft opening. It stands for the winding tower at the top of a mine shaft.

miner-safety-lamp.context: An old flame safety lamp with a mesh cage, a solid base and a ring on top. It stands for coal mining history and gas detection underground.

sluice-box.context: A sloping trough with riffle bars across its floor and water drops falling onto it. It stands for gold panning and placer mining.

bucket-wheel-excavator.context: A crawler machine with a long boom carrying a large wheel of buckets at its tip. It stands for giant surface mining machines used for coal and ore.

metal-ingot.context: A stack of three trapezoid metal bars, two below and one on top. It stands for gold bars, steel ingots and refined metal from a foundry.

pump-jack.context: A nodding oil pump with a walking beam on an A-frame, a horse head at one end and a crank wheel at the other. It stands for onshore oil wells.

offshore-oil-platform.context: A platform deck on tall legs standing in water with a derrick on top and a flare boom sticking out. It stands for offshore drilling and production.

wellhead.context: A stack of valves on a pipe rising from the ground, with handwheels branching off to both sides. It is the christmas tree assembly that controls an oil or gas well.

tricone-drill-bit.context: A drill bit with three toothed cones at the bottom of a threaded shank. It stands for rock drilling in oil, gas and mining.

roll-cage.context: A tall wire mesh cage cart with shelves and four casters. It stands for roll containers used in retail and distribution.

stacking-bin.context: An open-fronted plastic storage bin with a hand slot in its lip, stacked on a second bin. It stands for parts bins and picking bins in workshops and warehouses.

straddle-carrier.context: A tall narrow frame on wheels carrying a shipping container between its legs. It stands for container handling at ports and terminals.

reach-stacker.context: A heavy wheeled vehicle with a long angled boom holding a container from above at its tip. It stands for container handling in yards and terminals.

stretch-wrap-roll.context: A roll of clear plastic film on a core with handles, with the film unwinding to one side. It stands for wrapping pallets and parcels for shipping.

packing-tape-gun.context: A handheld tape dispenser with a pistol grip, a large tape roll and a serrated cutting edge. It stands for sealing boxes and parcels.

this-way-up.context: Two upward arrows standing on a base line, the packaging mark for keeping a parcel upright. It is printed on boxes and crates for shipping.

center-of-gravity.context: A circle divided into four quarters with two opposite quarters filled. It marks the center of gravity or center of mass on loads and in physics.

flow-meter.context: A short pipe section with flanges at both ends and a round dial display on top. It stands for measuring how much fluid passes through a pipe.

u-tube-manometer.context: A U-shaped glass tube with liquid standing at different heights in each arm. It stands for pressure measurement in labs and ventilation work.

sight-glass.context: A vertical glass tube between two small valves on a tank wall, showing a liquid level. It stands for level gauges on tanks, boilers and process vessels.

coordinate-measuring-machine.context: A granite table with a bridge frame over it and a vertical probe ending in a small ball tip. It stands for precision inspection of manufactured parts.

circular-knitting-machine.context: A round rack of thread cones above a cylinder, with a knitted fabric tube coming out underneath. It stands for textile and garment knitting.

pick-and-place-machine.context: A circuit board on a bed with a gantry head above it holding a tiny chip on a suction nozzle. It stands for surface-mount electronics assembly.

electric-arc-furnace.context: A round furnace vessel with a domed lid and three thick electrodes through it, with sparks below. It stands for steel making from scrap metal.

parabolic-trough-collector.context: A curved mirror trough on a stand with a receiver pipe at its focal line. It stands for solar thermal fields that heat fluid for power.

wave-energy-converter.context: A chain of jointed floating tube segments riding over wave lines. It stands for machines that make electricity from sea waves.

pumped-hydro-storage.context: A high reservoir and a low reservoir joined by a pipe running through a small turbine house. It stands for storing energy by moving water uphill.

kaplan-turbine.context: A propeller-like runner with broad blades at the bottom of a vertical shaft. It stands for low-head hydropower turbines in rivers and dams.

carbon-capture.context: A chimney with an arrow leading down through ground layers into underground storage. It stands for capturing and storing carbon dioxide from industry.

electrolyzer.context: A tank of water with two electrodes, rising bubbles and two gas pipes leaving the top. It stands for splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen.

wood-pellets.context: A small heap of short cylindrical wood pellets with two loose pellets in front. It stands for pellet fuel used in stoves and biomass boilers.
